passage: There are three main types of financial stress people encounter. The first type is apparent in people being stressed about the  {{1}} ups and downs of investment markets—actually not so much the ups, but {{2}}  the downs. These people are usually unable or unprepared to endure the long haul. The next common type of financial stress is that caused by debt. In a  {{3}} percentage of cases of debt-induced financial stress, credit cards and loans will be a central element. Often there will be a car loan and perhaps a mortgage, but credit cards often seem to be the gateway to debt-related financial difficulties for many. The third type of stress and  {{4}} the least known is inherited financial stress, which is the most destructive. It is experienced by those who have grown up in households where their parents regularly {{5}}  and fought about money. Money therefore becomes a stressful topic, and so the thought of sitting down and planning is an unattractive {{6}}  . Those suffering inherited financial anxiety {{7}}  to follow one of two patterns. Either they put their head in the sand: they would  {{8}} examining their financial statements, budgeting and discussing financial matters with those closest to them. Alternatively, they would go to the other {{9}}  , and micro-analyze everything, to the point of complete {{10}}  . They are convinced that whatever decision they make will be the wrong one.
